# Vercel AI SDK example

Audits a trace emitted by the [Vercel AI SDK](https://sdk.vercel.ai)'s
OpenTelemetry instrumentation.

## Run it

```bash
npm run build            # from the repo root
node examples/vercel-ai-sdk/audit.mjs
```

This reads [`trace.json`](./trace.json), prints a scored report, and writes
`report.html`.

## How the trace was produced

Enable telemetry on any AI SDK call and export the spans (OTLP/JSON) to a file
or collector:

```ts
import { generateText } from 'ai'
import { openai } from '@ai-sdk/openai'

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: openai('gpt-4o'),
  prompt: 'Research the latest agent frameworks.',
  tools: { /* ... */ },
  experimental_telemetry: { isEnabled: true, functionId: 'research-agent' },
})
```

agent-house reads the `ai.*` span attributes the SDK emits
(`ai.model.id`, `ai.usage.promptTokens`, `ai.toolCall.name`, …). It treats the
`ai.generateText.doGenerate` leaves as the real LLM calls and the
`ai.generateText` wrappers as chain spans, so token usage is never
double-counted.

## In code

```ts
import { audit } from 'agent-house'
const report = audit(traceJson) // format auto-detected
console.log(report.score, report.audits)
```

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node: [18, 20, 22]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run build
      # The CLI dogfoods itself: gate this repo's own demo trace.
      - run: node dist/cli.js assert examples/before-after/optimized.json --min-score 80

# 🏠 agent-house

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/agent-house.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/agent-house)
[![CI](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-house/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-house/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE)

> **Lighthouse for agents** - score an agent run, then tell it how to get faster and cheaper.

The ecosystem is full of *tracers* (Langfuse, LangSmith, Opik) that show you
**what happened**. `agent-house` is a **profiler**: it ingests an agent run
trace and produces a scored report (cost, latency, reliability, context-hygiene)
with concrete, ranked fixes - redundant tool calls, missed parallelization,
oversized context, uncached retrievals, model-tier mismatches - each with an
estimated **$ / ms saved** and a code-level hint.

It's a build-time tool: a **CLI + library + static HTML report**. Zero required
backend, zero runtime dependencies.

```
  agent-house - before / after

  naive ReAct agent     score 72/100   cost $0.245   7.0s
  after top-3 fixes     score 100/100   cost $0.024   2.0s

  ▲ +28 points · saved $0.221 and 5.0s per run
```

---

## Install

```bash
npm install agent-house        # library
npx agent-house run trace.json # or just run the CLI
```

Requires Node 18+. Ships as ESM with TypeScript types.

## Quick start

### CLI

```bash
# Score a trace and print a report (+ optional HTML/JSON output)
npx agent-house run ./trace.json --out report.html --json report.json

# Fail CI when the score drops below a threshold
npx agent-house assert ./trace.json --min-score 80

# Compare against a saved baseline report and gate on regressions
npx agent-house ci ./trace.json --baseline ./baseline.json --min-score 80
```

### Library

```ts
import { audit } from 'agent-house'

const report = await audit(trace)
// {
//   score: 72,
//   categories: [{ category: 'cost', score: 77, ... }, ...],
//   audits: [{ id, title, category, score, savings: { usd, ms }, findings, hint }, ...],
//   savings: { usd: 0.235, ms: 6400 },
//   run: { source, durationMs, spans, llmCalls, toolCalls, tokens, totalCostUsd },
// }

import { renderHtml, parseTrace } from 'agent-house'
const run = parseTrace(trace)
const html = renderHtml(audit(run), run) // self-contained, Lighthouse-style
```

`audit()` accepts a **raw trace** (auto-detected) or an already-normalized run.

## Supported trace formats

Ingest is built on the **OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions**, with thin
adapters for popular agent frameworks. Format is auto-detected.

| Framework | Format | Detected as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **OpenTelemetry GenAI** | OTLP/JSON with `gen_ai.*` attributes | `otel` |
| **Vercel AI SDK** | OTLP/JSON with `ai.*` attributes | `vercel` |
| **LangGraph / LangSmith** | LangSmith run tree (nested or flat) | `langgraph` |
| **Google ADK** | OTLP/JSON with `gcp.vertex.agent.*` | `adk` |

Read from a JSON file (CLI) or pass parsed JSON (library). See
[`examples/`](./examples) for a runnable example per framework.

## Scores

Each run gets four category scores (0–100) and a weighted **overall** score:

| Category | Default weight | What it measures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Cost** | 0.30 | wasted spend - wrong model tier, uncached prompts, bloat |
| **Latency** | 0.30 | wall-clock waste - duplicate and serial-when-parallelizable calls |
| **Reliability** | 0.20 | errors, retries, and loops |
| **Context** | 0.20 | oversized prompts relative to a healthy budget |

Weights are configurable (`audit(trace, { weights })`).

## Audits

| Audit | Category | Flags |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `duplicate-tool-calls` | latency | identical tool calls repeated in a run |
| `parallelizable-tool-calls` | latency | independent calls run serially that could be `Promise.all` |
| `model-tier-mismatch` | cost | a frontier model used for a trivial step |
| `uncacheable-prompts` | cost | large prompts re-sent across calls without caching |
| `errors` | reliability | spans that ended in an error |
| `retry-loops` | reliability | immediate retries and repeated-call loops |
| `context-bloat` | context | LLM calls sending oversized context |

Every audit returns a 0–1 score, the specific spans it flagged, an estimated
saving, and a **code-level hint** for the fix.

## The report

- **JSON** - the full structured report (the value `audit()` returns).
- **Static HTML** - a self-contained, Lighthouse-style page (inline CSS, no
  external assets, no backend) with score gauges and an SVG span **waterfall**.
  The report JSON is embedded in the page, so it doubles as a portable artifact.

## Configuration

```ts
audit(trace, {
  format: 'auto',            // 'otel' | 'vercel' | 'langgraph' | 'adk'
  models: [/* ModelPrice */],// override the price table with your negotiated rates
  thresholds: { contextBloatTokens: 12000 },
  weights: { cost: 0.4, latency: 0.3, reliability: 0.2, context: 0.1 },
})
```

The built-in price table covers Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, and xAI Grok
(standard-tier list prices, as of 2026-06; older model ids still resolve to the
nearest current entry). **The $/ms estimates are only as credible as this
table**, so it's fully overridable.

## How accurate are the savings?

The savings are **estimates** and may overlap across audits (a duplicate call is
also "extra latency"). They're designed to be directionally credible and to rank
fixes by impact - not to be exact invoices. The per-run **cost** and **duration**
totals come straight from the trace and are exact.

## Non-goals (MVP)

No hosted dashboard, no continuous monitoring, no auto-fix. It's a build-time
tool: a CLI + library + static report, not a SaaS.

## Architecture

```
trace (OTLP / Vercel / LangGraph / ADK)
        │  ingest adapters → normalize
        ▼
   AgentRun (spans: kind, timing, model, usage, …)
        │
        ├─ pricing engine  → cost per span
        ├─ audits          → findings + savings + hints
        └─ scoring         → category + overall scores
        ▼
   Report  →  JSON  +  static HTML (gauges + waterfall)
```

Adding a framework is one adapter that normalizes to `AgentRun`; nothing
downstream changes.

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). The project is test-driven - every
feature lands with Vitest tests. Run `npm test`.

# The demo that sells it - before / after

Take a real, naive ReAct agent, score it, apply the top fixes, and re-score.

## Run it

```bash
npm run build            # from the repo root
node examples/before-after/compare.mjs
```

```
  agent-house - before / after

  naive ReAct agent     score 72/100   cost $0.245   7.0s
  after top-3 fixes     score 100/100   cost $0.024   2.0s

  ▲ +28 points
  saved $0.221 and 5.0s per run
```

It also writes `naive.html` and `optimized.html` - open them side by side to
compare the score gauges and span waterfalls.

## What changed

[`naive.json`](./naive.json) is a trace full of the inefficiencies agents
accumulate in the wild:

- **Duplicate tool calls** - `web_search` fired 3× with identical input.
- **Serial calls** - `fetch_url`, `query_db`, `scrape` awaited one-by-one.
- **Model-tier mismatch** - trivial routing/classification on a frontier model.
- **Uncacheable prompts** - a large prompt re-sent every synthesis turn.
- **Context bloat** - 12–13k input tokens per call.
- **An error + retry** on an overloaded model.

[`optimized.json`](./optimized.json) applies the fixes: route on a cheap model,
run the independent tools concurrently, cache the shared prefix, trim context,
and drop the duplicates. The composite score climbs and the per-run cost falls
by ~90%.

> Savings are estimates and may overlap across audits; the per-run cost and
> duration deltas above come straight from the two traces.

# LangGraph / LangSmith example

Audits a [LangGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/) run exported as a
[LangSmith](https://smith.langchain.com) run tree.

## Run it

```bash
npm run build            # from the repo root
node examples/langgraph/audit.mjs
```

Reads [`trace.json`](./trace.json), prints a scored report, writes `report.html`.

## How the trace was produced

LangGraph runs are traced by LangSmith. With tracing enabled
(`LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=true`, `LANGCHAIN_API_KEY=...`), every run is captured as a
tree of `run_type` nodes (`chain`, `llm`, `tool`, `retriever`). Export a run via
the LangSmith SDK/API to get the JSON used here - either a single root run with
nested `child_runs`, or a flat array of runs linked by `parent_run_id`. Both
shapes are supported.

agent-house maps `run_type` to span kinds and pulls token usage from both
common LangChain shapes (`outputs.llm_output.token_usage` and
`outputs.usage_metadata`), plus the model/provider from
`extra.invocation_params` / `extra.metadata`.

## In code

```ts
import { audit } from 'agent-house'
const report = audit(runTreeJson) // detected as LangGraph/LangSmith
```

# Google ADK example

Audits a trace from the [Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/),
which exports OpenTelemetry spans.

## Run it

```bash
npm run build            # from the repo root
node examples/adk/audit.mjs
```

Reads [`trace.json`](./trace.json), prints a scored report, writes `report.html`.

## How the trace was produced

ADK emits OpenTelemetry spans using the `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions plus
`gcp.vertex.agent.*` attributes, with span names like `invocation`,
`agent_run [name]`, `call_llm`, and `execute_tool [name]`. Wire up any OTLP
exporter (console, file, or a collector) in your ADK app and capture the
exported spans as OTLP/JSON.

agent-house reuses its GenAI interpretation and refines ADK's span-name
vocabulary and payload attributes (`gcp.vertex.agent.tool_call_args`,
`gcp.vertex.agent.llm_response`, …).

## In code

```ts
import { audit } from 'agent-house'
const report = audit(otlpJson) // detected as ADK
```
